title: Continuous cochains compute derived invariants for discrete profinite modules
statement: Let $G$ be a profinite group, $A$ a finite ring, and $M$ a left $A$-module with a $G$-action by $A$-linear automorphisms such that every element has open stabilizer. In the abelian category of such modules with $A$-linear $G$-equivariant maps [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian], let $H^q(G,M)$ be the $q$-th right derived functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive], in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], of $M\mapsto M^G$. Give $M$ the discrete topology. For every $q\geq0$, $H^q(G,M)$ is naturally isomorphic to degree-$q$ cohomology of the inhomogeneous cochain complex $C^n(G,M)=\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M)$, where $d^0m(g)=gm-m$ and, for $n\geq1$, $d^nf(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^jf(g_1,\ldots,g_jg_{j+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$.

proof.text: Write $T^q(M)=H^q(C^\bullet(G,M))$. The displayed differentials are natural in equivariant $A$-linear maps. For every short exact sequence of discrete $G$-modules, [lem-exc-continuous-cochains-short-exact] gives a short exact sequence of these complexes. Apply the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] and its compatibility with morphisms of short exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality]. Thus $(T^q)$ is a cohomological $\delta$-functor [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor]. At degree zero, $\ker(d^0)$ consists exactly of elements fixed by every $g\in G$, and $T^0(M)=M^G$ naturally. The same kernel description and exactness in [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian] show that invariants are left exact and additive.

proof.text: For each $M$, [lem-exc-coinduced-discrete-embedding] supplies a monomorphism $\iota_M:M\to D(M)=\operatorname{Cont}(G,M)$ in this abelian category, with the right-translation action. For every $q>0$, [lem-exc-coinduced-continuous-acyclic] gives $T^q(D(M))=0$. Hence $T^q(\iota_M):T^q(M)\to T^q(D(M))$ is the zero map, so $T$ is effaceable in every positive degree.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, label section-continuous-group-cohomology, final profinite comparison asserted without a proof; agent-written effacement argument

proof.text: By Step 1, $T$ is a cohomological $\delta$-functor; by Step 2 it satisfies the monomorphism-and-zero-map hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal], so $T$ is universal. The category has enough injectives by [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian], and invariants are left exact by Step 1. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] applies to invariants: its derived functors $R^q(M\mapsto M^G)$ form a universal $\delta$-functor with $R^0\cong(M\mapsto M^G)$.

proof.text: Identify $R^0$ and $T^0$ with the invariant functor by Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor]. Universality of $R^\bullet$ gives a unique morphism $R^\bullet\to T^\bullet$ extending the identity on invariants; universality of $T^\bullet$ gives one in the reverse direction. Each composite extends the identity in degree zero, so uniqueness makes both composites identities. The first morphism is therefore a natural isomorphism in every degree.
